reconcile.note: Adam Clarke reads the death-appointed-once rule as covering humanity in general, explicitly carving out Enoch and Elijah as recorded exceptions.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Must everyone die?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/die.html) (1999).

sides.snippet: Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him.
sides.verseText: Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him.
